newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber close off limit second day to new lows.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber close off limit second day to new lows.

text.p: Carryover stop loss selling from Friday's limit losses along with further fund selling and general long liquidation pushed CME lumber futures down the $10.00 per tbf daily limit for the second day to new contract lows in all months, traders said.

Lumber close down the $10.00 limit in all but March with July at $347.10 and September at $344.00 per tbf. All months set new lows and the daily limit is expanded to $15.00 Tuesday due to the two consecutive declines in July.
Renwed selling developed after early short covering failed to followthrough with fund selling evident, traders said.

"You had fund selling again today, obviously margin call liquidation near the opening, and when the (short covering) didn't hold this morning you had further selling, both liquidation and new shorts being put on," said Curt Cunningham, President of Pacific Futures Trading.

Cunningham noted that with the expanded limit Tuesday futures could go down to near last major low in the market of $328 set last September. However, the market is oversold compared to cash prices, even if cash is falling, he said.
"Your equivalent of $335 cash two-by-four and I don't know anywhere where you could buy two-by-four at that price in the cash market," Cunningham added.
Cash sources reported spruce trading in the $350 per tbf area. Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $358 per tbf Friday, the lowest price level since July 19, 1996.
